Replay

Native Quickdraw saves

2 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

The native session menu accepts a save-file path and offers Resume solo and Resume host. During a direct authority session, Save/F5 writes the complete authority checkpoint. A connected client or observer cannot save authority state. Explicit scripted launches can use RQ_SAVE=/path/duel.replay RQ_RESUME=1 RQ_ROLE=host or RQ_ROLE=solo; RQ_PROFILE selects the local reconnect identity separately.

The checkpoint contains the complete world: player lives/HP, scores, gold/equipment, drone positions, cooldowns, respawn deadlines, active lobs, collision history, names and start policy. Session identities, input/action ledgers and their accepted pending work are part of the shared archive format. It does not save scene nodes, active cosmetic pulses, local chat scrollback or personal profile files.

Resume validates the model/content contract and the saving host's identity before opening a new authority session. It starts a newer epoch from the exact saved frame. Direct file resume uses the default retirement policy for accepted but unexecuted commands and schedules absent peers to leave; matching identities can rejoin their retained seats. It does not resurrect old network connections or silently preserve pending purchases. Solo resume keeps the host and lets other saved players depart. Presentation is freshly seeded so historical shots/hurt flashes/rings do not replay.

A local file is not a host-election credential. Quickdraw refuses file resume for configured Room sessions and for permit/custom-policy archives; those require their recovery service. File resume deliberately creates a new direct session. Stop the old direct game before replacing it. Configured online authorities now publish through Room; public deployment remains separate work. Abandoned-party restoration now has its own service-backed acceptance path.

Writes use the existing bounded staged-file/rename helper. A failed write leaves the previous committed file intact. Missing, damaged, incompatible or wrong-owner files do not open a session and show a specific menu explanation. This is the existing process-crash save boundary, not a new portable power-loss durability guarantee. Native identity and display-name preferences remain separate; do not share an identity file as a game-save export.

The game content/schema remains D2; this feature does not add gameplay fields. D1 archives still have no implicit conversion. Browser IndexedDB slots and identity persistence now have their own browser-local flow; they do not use native file paths.

Run tests/replay_quickdraw_save/run.sh from the Nix development environment for a fresh-process combat save/resume fixture. It uses isolated paths and identities, kills only its owned writers after a durable receipt, checks negative loads and failed-write preservation, then continues respawn, equipment, purchases, lobs and named chat in a fresh host/client pair.
